title: A rotating alphabet with a separator clock
question: Does the archived two-clock progressive alphabet reach its own frequency gate on its named LP2 targets?
reader_question: Could the word separators tell a rotating alphabet when to turn?
summary: No source-selected LP2 page reaches the archived program's 1.4 IoC gate under either its literal parser or a declared corrected-rune variant.
finding: Across eleven actual LP2 targets, all 1,682 distinct effective schedules per page yield zero outputs above the source's normalized-IoC 1.4 gate with either parser. The highest LP2 values are 1.164 (literal parser) and 1.159 (canonical correction). The source's twelfth named page is solved LP1-15; its literal parser yields two gated outputs but its corrected parser yields none. Eight known-reading plants recover and pass the gate; none of 49 whole-search page-shuffle controls passes either.
limitations: The source parser omits canonical ᛄ; corrected parsing is a new bounded variant rather than unchanged historical execution. Its old page 15 is solved LP1-15 and excluded from the unsolved-page maximum. The 49 shuffles provide no calibrated probability with zero gated maxima. A constant starting phase cannot alter IoC; nonzero-phase readings were not separately scored. No plaintext language, extra layer or general changing-alphabet family is ruled out.
next_steps: A new separator-clock proposal should state its glyph parser and page identities, and predict a readable held-out passage before tuning further shifts.

scope.representation: Pinned old Wulfic page files with exact source parser and a separate canonical-GP rune correction. Old page15 is solved LP1-15 control only.
scope.procedure: Enumerate all source directions, two shifts and three modes, deduplicate 5,046 named settings to 1,682 effective outputs, score source normalized IoC and above-gate bigrams/trigrams on each of eleven LP2 targets. Repeat complete search on 49 pagewise shuffled controls for each parser.
scope.parameters: 11 LP2 pages plus one solved LP1 source target; 2 parsers; 29 rune shifts × 29 separator shifts × 2 directions × 3 modes; 49 complete-search shuffles; seed 330123.
scope.exclusions: Other source pages, nonzero-phase readings (the IoC gate is invariant to constant phase), new separator rules, key switching, other alphabets, extra encryption layers and general Alberti disk mechanisms.

review.kind: source-defined finite grid and declared corrected-parser sensitivity
review.reviewer: 24 source/adapter parity cases, eight recovered known-reading plants, independent reconstruction of 24 observed page and 98 whole-search control results

reproduction.environment: Python 3 and NumPy; full source-parity gate also requires the pinned Wulfic checkout.

visuals.caption: Every LP2 page's best two-clock collision score remains below the archived source's 1.4 hit threshold.
